title: Golden Gate Bridge
blurb: A detailed procedural model of the 2,737 m Golden Gate Bridge: two 746 ft Art Deco towers, 7,650 ft main cables spun from 27,572 wires each, 250 suspender pairs with cable bands, the stiffening truss, the Fort Point arch, anchorages, toll plaza, and south tower foghorns.

sourceUrls.label: Golden Gate Bridge District: Facts and Figures
Golden Gate Bridge District: NTSB statement
Golden Gate Bridge District: Art Deco Style

systems.name: North tower
systems.description: Marin side tower. Art Deco steel tower rising 746 ft above the water, with stepped back legs, four portals, fluted housings, and portal cross bracing.

systems.name: South tower
systems.description: San Francisco side tower. Art Deco steel tower rising 746 ft above the water, with stepped back legs, four portals, fluted housings, chevron ornament, and portal cross bracing.

systems.name: Tower piers and fender
systems.description: Tower foundations and the south fender. The south pier is anchored to bedrock beneath the water; the north pier stands half on land and half in water.

systems.name: Main cables
systems.description: The two main cables, each 36 3/8 in in diameter and 7,650 ft long, spun from 27,572 wires.

systems.name: Cable bands
systems.description: Steel bands clamped around the main cables at each suspender attachment, carrying the suspender sockets. Band positions follow the schematic suspender spacing.

systems.name: Suspender ropes
systems.description: 250 pairs of vertical suspender ropes hang the roadway from the two main cables.

systems.name: Stiffening truss and bracing
systems.description: The stiffening truss plus the lateral and diagonal bracing retrofitted in 1953 to 1954 to keep the deck rigid.

systems.name: Deck, lanes, and walkways
systems.description: The 90 ft wide deck with six lanes of US 101 and SR 1, two walkways, railings, and a movable median barrier.

systems.name: Roadway markings and joints
systems.description: Dashed lane dividers for the six lanes and expansion joints at the towers. Marking and joint geometry is schematic.

systems.name: Anchorages
systems.description: Concrete blocks that fix the main cables at each end of the bridge.

systems.name: Fort Point arch and approaches
systems.description: The steel arch over Fort Point, the approach viaducts, and the angular entrance pylons.

systems.name: Toll plaza, lighting, and signals
systems.description: The southern toll plaza, the Art Deco light standards, and the south tower foghorns.

systems.name: Maintenance access
systems.description: Under deck rails and maintenance travelers for inspection and repair. Rail and traveler layout is schematic; the bridge is continuously maintained, with 38 painters keeping up the paintwork.

explanations.east walkway: The main walkway is on the eastern side, used by pedestrians and bicycles at different hours. Railings between the walkways and the traffic lanes were added in 2003. Walkway geometry is schematic.
